newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-MACKERDHUJ HITS OUT AT SUB-STANDARD TEST GROUNDS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MACKERDHUJ HITS OUT AT SUB-STANDARD TEST GROUNDS.

text.p: Krish Mackerdhuj, president of the United Cricket Board of South Africa, called on the sport's controlling body on Wednesday to crack down on sub-standard test grounds.
Mackerdhuj was particularly critical of Ahmedabad where India beat South Africa in the first test by 64 runs last month.
"I believe in order to preserve test cricket -- and to play it at the highest level -- one has to provide wickets at test venues that are of test standard," Mackerdhuj said in an interview.

"I believe that the ICC (International Cricket Council) must come out strongly in this regard. We have a playing affairs committee and we have match referees who will report on venues and other related matters. What we also need are pitch inspectors going around to check the wickets
"And this shouldn't present any problems at all. At world level, with flying from one country to another so easy, we must fly out people who can inspect these wickets if there's a problem."
Mackerdhuj singled out Ahmedabad as typical of a sub-standard test venue.

"I have no doubt about it. I will say quite openly that the Ahmedabad wicket was not of the type of standard we would like to see in test cricket. One simply shouldn't see dust coming out of a wicket on the first day.

"I don't mind countries having wickets that are suited to their players, but they must still be of test standard. We know that the sub-continent wickets take a lot of spin because of their slowness, but that is not the problem.
"The problem there was a wicket which was not prepared for test standard, it was one that crumbled on the first day and that gave off dust."
